OXT in Interoception - Part II

Author

Natascha Stoffel

Published

June 13, 2026

Information on the Data

BASEC registration number : 2023-0469

Study Visit “Interoception” conducted between 18.10.2023 - 4.9.2024, with completed N=92 participants.

In this analysis we will be looking at the RedCap data that is downloaded from the redcapmed.unifr.ch server, with project number PID 121, named “Interoception” in correlation with the Oxytocin Saliva Samples that were taken at specific time points.

Part I for the behavioural and saliva samples can be found in the other markdown.

This is v2 of the script, which was adapted after the discussion with Hugo Najberg.

with acknowledgment to Samantha Weber for sharing the original code https://github.com/webersamantha/Oxytocin_FND

# 1. Load Data -----------------------------------------------------------------

# Read in the data
# genetics (SNPs)
df_genetics <- read_excel("/Users/nataschastoffel/Documents/GitHub/interoception_NS/data/processed/08-2025/genetics_SNPs.xlsx")
df_genetics$pcode <- sub("^P00", "", df_genetics$pcode) # gets rid of the P00 for all participants
df_genetics$pcode <- sub("^P0", "", df_genetics$pcode) # gets rid of the P0 for all participants
df_genetics$pcode <- sub("^P", "", df_genetics$pcode) # gets rid of the P for all participants

# epigenetics (methylation)
df_epigenetics <- read_excel("/Users/nataschastoffel/Documents/GitHub/interoception_NS/data/processed/08-2025/epigenetics_OXTRmethylation.xlsx")
df_epigenetics$pcode <- sub("^P00", "", df_epigenetics$pcode) # gets rid of the P00 for all participants
df_epigenetics$pcode <- sub("^P0", "", df_epigenetics$pcode) # gets rid of the P0 for all participants
df_epigenetics$pcode <- sub("^P", "", df_epigenetics$pcode) # gets rid of the P for all participants

df_OXTR<-merge(df_genetics, df_epigenetics, x.by=c("pcode"),y.by=c("pcode"),all.x=TRUE, all.y=TRUE) # merges the files

# Create an average methylation score for the CpG sites
df_OXTR$OXTR_intron_CpG_average <- rowMeans(
  df_OXTR[, c("OXTR_intron_CpG_2", "OXTR_intron_CpG_5", "OXTR_intron_CpG_6.7", "OXTR_intron_CpG_8")],  na.rm = TRUE)

df_OXTR$OXTR_promoter_CpG_average <- rowMeans(
  df_OXTR[, c("OXTR_promoter_CpG_2", "OXTR_promoter_CpG_3", "OXTR_promoter_CpG_4", "OXTR_promoter_CpG_5.6", "OXTR_promoter_CpG_8")],  na.rm = TRUE)


# CRF (all other data)
df_CRF <- read_excel("/Users/nataschastoffel/Documents/GitHub/interoception_NS/data/processed/08-2025/Data.CRF_FINAL_20241218.xlsx")

df_CRF <- df_CRF %>%
  mutate(anx_dep_SUM = stai_t + bdi)

df_CRF <- df_CRF %>%
  mutate(medication_brain = if_else(psychotropic_medication == 1 | sleep_benzo == 1 | pain_antiepi == 1 | pain_morph_opio == 1, 1, 0))  

df_FULL<-merge(df_CRF, df_OXTR, x.by=c("pcode"),y.by=c("pcode"),all.x=TRUE, all.y=TRUE) # merges the files

# Summary of missing data per SNP
colSums(is.na(df_FULL[, c("rs2254298", "rs53576")])) # 3 missing data

# Show pcode of missing SNPS
missing_snps <- df_FULL[is.na(df_FULL$rs2254298) | is.na(df_FULL$rs53576), ] 
missing_snps[, c("pcode", "rs2254298", "rs53576")] # MISSING: P047, P049, P093
# exclude missing data at two two SNPs (to have complete genetic dataset as df)
df <- df_FULL[!df_FULL$pcode %in% c("47", "49", "93"), ]

# Show pcode of missing methylation values
missing_methyl <- df[is.na(df$OXTR_intron_CpG_2) | is.na(df$OXTR_intron_CpG_5) | is.na(df$OXTR_intron_CpG_6.7) | is.na(df$OXTR_intron_CpG_8) | is.na(df$OXTR_promoter_CpG_2) | is.na(df$OXTR_promoter_CpG_3) | is.na(df$OXTR_promoter_CpG_4) | is.na(df$OXTR_promoter_CpG_5.6) | is.na(df$OXTR_promoter_CpG_8), ] 
missing_methyl[, c("pcode")] # no missing

# Make individual dataframes
df_FND<-filter(df, group =="1")
df_HC<-filter(df, group =="0")

### upload dataframe with salivary OXT (excluding missing/ outliers)
df_OT <- read_excel("/Users/nataschastoffel/Documents/GitHub/interoception_NS/data/processed/08-2025/df_OXT_FULL.xlsx")

# merge OXT and genetic dataset
dfOT_FULL<-merge(df_OT, df_OXTR, x.by=c("pcode"),y.by=c("pcode"),all.x=TRUE, all.y=TRUE) # merges the files
# exclude missing data for the two SNPs (to have complete genetic dataset as df OT as well "47", "49", "93" but also those with missing/outlier variables in salivary OT: "2", "9"
df_OT <- dfOT_FULL[!dfOT_FULL$pcode %in% c("2", "9", "47", "49", "93"), ]

df_OT$Oxytocin <- rowMeans(df_OT[, c("Oxytocin_waking", "Oxytocin_lunch", "Oxytocin_pretask", "Oxytocin_posttask")], na.rm = TRUE)


# Make individual dataframes
dfOT_FND<-filter(df_OT, group =="1")
dfOT_HC<-filter(df_OT, group =="0")

# Create a new dataset to do sex specific analysis
dfOT_female<-filter(df_OT, sex =="1")

# Create no-medication dataset
df_nomed <- df %>%filter(medication_brain == 0)
df_nomed <- merge(df_nomed,df_OT[, c("pcode","Oxytocin")],by = "pcode",all.x = TRUE)
dfOT_nomed <- df_nomed[!df_nomed$pcode %in% c("2", "9", "47", "49", "93"), ]

#### EXTENDED statistics on demographics table:

df_tbl <- df %>%
  mutate(sex = factor(  sex, levels = c("1", "2"),  labels = c("female", "male") ),
    group = factor(group,levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("HC", "FND")),
    psychotropic_medication = factor(psychotropic_medication, levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("no", "yes")))

Data.t <- df_tbl %>%
  select(group,sex,age,psychotropic_medication,bdi,stai_t,ctq_total)

format_p <- function(p) {ifelse(  is.na(p), NA_character_,  ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))}
format_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {ifelse(is.na(x),NA_character_,sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))}

# Welch t-test:
# statistic = t
# df = Welch-Satterthwaite df
# effect size = Cohen's d
# CI = mean difference CI and Cohen's d CI

get_ttest_stats <- function(data, var) {
  
  f <- as.formula(paste(var, "~ group"))
  test <- t.test(f, data = data)
  d <- effectsize::cohens_d(f,data = data,ci = 0.95)
  
  tibble(variable = var,
         row_type = "label",
         test_used = "Welch t-test",
         test_statistic = paste0(
      "t = ",
      format_num(unname(test$statistic), 2)
    ),
    df = format_num(unname(test$parameter), 2),
    effect_size = paste0(
      "d = ",
      format_num(d$Cohens_d, 2)
    ),
    effect_size_ci = paste0(
      "[",
      format_num(d$CI_low, 2),
      ", ",
      format_num(d$CI_high, 2),
      "]"
    ),
    ci = paste0(
      "Mean difference 95% CI [",
      format_num(test$conf.int[1], 2),
      ", ",
      format_num(test$conf.int[2], 2),
      "]"
    )
  )
}


# Wilcoxon rank-sum test:
# statistic = W
# df = not applicable
# effect size = Cohen's d
# CI = Hodges-Lehmann CI and Cohen's d CI

get_wilcox_stats <- function(data, var) {
  
  f <- as.formula(paste(var, "~ group"))
  test <- wilcox.test(f,data = data,exact = FALSE,conf.int = TRUE)
  d <- effectsize::cohens_d(f,data = data,ci = 0.95)
  
  tibble(
    variable = var,
    row_type = "label",
    test_used = "Wilcoxon rank-sum test",
    test_statistic = paste0(
      "W = ",
      format_num(unname(test$statistic), 2)
    ),
    df = NA_character_,
    effect_size = paste0(
      "d = ",
      format_num(d$Cohens_d, 2)
    ),
    effect_size_ci = paste0(
      "[",
      format_num(d$CI_low, 2),
      ", ",
      format_num(d$CI_high, 2),
      "]"
    ),
    ci = paste0(
      "Hodges-Lehmann 95% CI [",
      format_num(test$conf.int[1], 2),
      ", ",
      format_num(test$conf.int[2], 2),
      "]"
    )
  )
}

# Fisher's exact test:
# statistic and df are not applicable
# effect size = Odds Ratio
# additional estimate = Cramer's V with 95% CI

get_fisher_stats <- function(data, var) {
  tab <- table(data[[var]], data$group)
  test <- fisher.test(tab)
  cv <- effectsize::cramers_v(tab,ci = 0.95)

  tibble(variable = var,
    row_type = "label",
    test_used = "Fisher's exact test",
    test_statistic = NA_character_,
    df = NA_character_,
    effect_size = paste0(
      "OR = ",
      format_num(unname(test$estimate), 2)
    ),
    effect_size_ci = paste0(
      "[",
      format_num(test$conf.int[1], 2),
      ", ",
      format_num(test$conf.int[2], 2),
      "]"
    ),
    ci = paste0(
      "Cramer's V = ",
      format_num(cv$Cramers_v, 2),
      " [",
      format_num(cv$CI_low, 2),
      ", ",
      format_num(cv$CI_high, 2),
      "]"
    )
  )
}

extra_stats <- bind_rows(
  get_fisher_stats(Data.t, "sex"),
  get_ttest_stats(Data.t, "age"),
  get_fisher_stats(Data.t, "psychotropic_medication"),
  get_wilcox_stats(Data.t, "bdi"),
  get_ttest_stats(Data.t, "stai_t"),
  get_wilcox_stats(Data.t, "ctq_total")
)

table_ext <- Data.t %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = group,
    missing = "no",
    statistic = list(
      sex ~ "{n} ({p})",
      age ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      psychotropic_medication ~ "{n} ({p})",
      bdi ~ "{median} ({IQR})",
      stai_t ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      ctq_total ~ "{median} ({IQR})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      sex ~ 1,
      age ~ 1,
      psychotropic_medication ~ 1,
      bdi ~ 1,
      stai_t ~ 1,
      ctq_total ~ 1
    ),
    label = list(
      sex ~ "Sex",
      age ~ "Age",
      psychotropic_medication ~ "Psychotropic medication",
      bdi ~ "Depression: BDI-II",
      stai_t ~ "Trait Anxiety: STAI-T",
      ctq_total ~ "Childhood Trauma: CTQ"
    )
  ) %>%
  add_overall(last = FALSE) %>%
  add_p(
    test = list(
      sex ~ "fisher.test",
      age ~ "t.test",
      psychotropic_medication ~ "fisher.test",

    label ~ "**Variable**",

    "**Table 1. Demographic and clinical characteristics with inferential statistics**"
  ) %>%

    p.value ~ "p-values are based on Welch t-tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, or Fisher's exact tests, as appropriate.",

    effect_size_ci ~ "Confidence intervals for Cohen's d are reported for continuous variables. For categorical variables, confidence intervals refer to odds ratios.",
    ci ~ "For Welch t-tests, confidence intervals refer to mean differences. For Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, confidence intervals refer to Hodges-Lehmann location shifts. For Fisher's exact tests, this column reports Cramer's V with 95% CI."
  )

## Quality control using Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium (HWE) 
# FUNDAMENTAL: CREATE setupSNP:
# we first specify which columns contain the genotyping data, and then what alleles they are without separation

# Identify SNP column indices by name
snp_cols <- which(names(df) %in% c("rs2254298", "rs53576"))
snp_cols_OT <- which(names(df_OT) %in% c("rs2254298", "rs53576"))

# Apply setupSNP with named columns
myData_S <- setupSNP(data = df, colSNPs = snp_cols, sep = "")

##  Association Analysis for two SNP -----------------------------------------
myData_S$group<-as.factor(myData_S$group)

# Check both genes at once first only age and sex as covariates 
# Using WGassociation to tests each SNP separately under multiple genetic inheritance models (codominant, dominant, recessive, log-additive), first without, then with adjusting for covariates.
asoc_S1<-WGassociation(group~1+ age + sex, data=myData_S, model=c("codominant","log-additive","dominant","recessive"), genotypingRate=80)

# Logistic regression with functions from SNPassoc:

##  Visualization -----------------------------------
# We run a repeated measures Anova on the fitted data. So first a glm, then an Anova on the glm data in order to have covariates included. 
df$group <- factor(df$group, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("HC", "FND"))

# Plot data for OXTR_intron_CpG_average
OXTRboxplot<-ggplot(df, aes(x=group, y=OXTR_intron_CpG_average, fill=group)) +
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme_classic()+  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#868686FF" ,"#BB4038"))+ 
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.y = element_blank(), 
        axis.title.x = element_blank()) +
  ggtitle(expression(italic("OXTR") ~ "Methylation Intron Region [%]")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 20, face = "bold"))+  
  theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))+ 
  stat_compare_means(label = "p.signif", comparisons = list(c("HC", "FND")), label.x=1)+ 
  geom_jitter(shape=16, position=position_jitter(0.2))
OXTRboxplot

### separate per site (instead of averaging)
df_introns <- df %>% select(pcode, group, starts_with("OXTR_intron_CpG_"))

df_long <- df_introns %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("OXTR_intron_CpG_"),
    names_to = "CpG_site",
    values_to = "methylation")
df_long <- df_long %>% mutate( group = factor(group),CpG_site = factor(CpG_site) )

## stat test
stat_test <- df_long %>%
  group_by(CpG_site) %>%
  wilcox_test(methylation ~ group) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "fdr") %>%
  add_significance()
stat_test

#### Statistical tests
vars_to_test <- c("Oxytocin", "OXTR_promoter_CpG_average", "OXTR_intron_CpG_average")

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis tests by group and variable
kw_results <- df_OT %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(vars_to_test), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value") %>% 
  group_by(group, outcome) %>% 
  kruskal_test(value ~ rs53576) %>% 
  adjust_pvalue(method = "fdr") %>% 
  add_significance() %>% 
  mutate( p_value = signif(p, 3),
    p_adj = signif(p.adj, 3)  ) %>% 
  select(group, outcome, statistic, p_value, p_adj, p.adj.signif)

# Show results

### sig results for intron OXTR in HC and sig reuslts for Oxytocin in FND

# run post hoc test for HC (OXTR_intron_CpG_average)
hc_posthoc <- dfOT_HC %>% 
  pairwise_wilcox_test( OXTR_intron_CpG_average ~ rs53576,p.adjust.method = "fdr")

# run post hoc test for FND (Oxytocin)
fnd_posthoc <- dfOT_FND %>% 
  pairwise_wilcox_test( Oxytocin ~ rs53576, p.adjust.method = "fdr" )

# Clean and view results
hc_posthoc <- hc_posthoc %>% 
  mutate(group = "HC", outcome = "OXTR_intron_CpG_average")

fnd_posthoc <- fnd_posthoc %>% 
  mutate(group = "FND", outcome = "Oxytocin")

# Combine and select relevant info
posthoc_results <- bind_rows(hc_posthoc, fnd_posthoc) %>% 
  mutate(
    p = signif(p, 3),
    p.adj = signif(p.adj, 3) ) %>% 
  select(group, outcome, group1, group2, p, p.adj, p.adj.signif)

4.1) Linear Regressions : three-way-interaction

Now we test whether there is a three-way interaction with these variables (predicting the hormonal variable of salivary OXT)

4.1.1) Intron Methylation

## make sure group is a factor
df_OT$group <- factor(df_OT$group)


# OXYTOCIN: group interacting with genotype and methylation
OXTRlm <- lm(formula = Oxytocin ~ group*rs53576*OXTR_intron_CpG_average,
             data = df_OT) 

OTAov <- aov(OXTRlm)
summary(OTAov) # significant group p = 0.0335 and signifincant interaction fo group and genotype (p = 0.0260), as well as sig interaction of genotype and methylation (p=0.0330). No three-way interaction

# Visualization
oxytocin_summary <- df_OT %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("HC", "FND"))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group, rs53576) %>%
  dplyr::summarise( n    = n(),
    mean = mean(Oxytocin, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = sd(Oxytocin, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
    t    = qt(1 - alpha/2, df = n - 1),
    ci   = t * se, .groups = "drop" )

pd_points <- position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.4)
pd_sum    <- position_dodge(width = 0.4)

# plotting
interaction_plot <- ggplot(df_OT,
  aes(x = factor(group, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("HC", "FND")), y = Oxytocin, color = rs53576)) +
  # Raw data (jittered individual data points)
  geom_point(position = pd_points, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +

  # Means connected by genotype
  geom_line( data = oxytocin_summary,
    aes(x = group, y = mean, group = rs53576, color = rs53576),
    position = pd_sum, linewidth = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE  ) +
  geom_point( data = oxytocin_summary,
    aes(x = group, y = mean, color = rs53576),
    position = pd_sum, size = 3, shape = 16, fill = "white", stroke = 1,
    inherit.aes = FALSE ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = oxytocin_summary,
    aes(x = group, ymin = mean - ci, ymax = mean + ci, color = rs53576),
    position = pd_sum, width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE ) +

  scale_color_manual(values = c("#3B7EBF", "#4DAF4A", "#E6B91E")) +
  labs(title = expression(italic("OXTR") ~ "Genotype × Group Interaction on Oxytocin"),
    x = "Group", y = "Salivary Oxytocin [pg/ml]",  color = "rs53576 Genotype" ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme( plot.title   = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)  )

interaction_plot

4.2) Linear Regressions : Replication (supplements)

We now want to replicate following two interaction findings of Weber & Stoffel et al, 2025:

  • group*genotype on OXTR intron methylation

  • group*methylation on OXT saliva

5) Interoception

Further analyses on existing interoceptive group differences with oxytocinergic variables

    ### exclusion for RRST (outlier)
    df_rrst <- df %>% filter(pcode != 63)
    df_rrst_OT <- df_OT %>% filter(pcode != 63) %>% mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("HC", "FND")))
    df_OT_plot <- df_OT %>% mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("HC", "FND")))  


## Respiratory Sensitivity
a <- ggscatter(df_rrst, x = "rrst_sensitivity", y = "OXTR_intron_CpG_average", fill = "group", color = "group",
               add = "reg.line", conf.int = TRUE, 
               cor.coef = FALSE, cor.method = "spearman",
               xlab = "Respiratory Sensitivity", ylab = "OXTR Intron Methylation [%]") + 
  stat_cor(aes(color = group), method = "spearman", 
           label.x = Inf, label.y = c(Inf, Inf), 
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = c(2, 4)) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#868686FF", "#BB4038")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#868686FF", "#BB4038"))

b <- ggscatter(df_rrst, x = "rrst_sensitivity", y = "OXTR_promoter_CpG_average", fill = "group", color = "group",
               add = "reg.line", conf.int = TRUE, 
               cor.coef = FALSE, cor.method = "spearman",
               xlab = "Respiratory Sensitivity", ylab = "OXTR Promoter Methylation [%]") + 
  stat_cor(aes(color = group), method = "spearman", 
           label.x = Inf, label.y = c(Inf, Inf), 
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = c(2, 4)) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#868686FF", "#BB4038")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#868686FF", "#BB4038"))

7) post-hoc sensitivity power analysis

# Case-control association: group ~ rs53576_add
# N = current complete genetic sample

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(writexl)

df_genetic_power <- df_OT %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      group %in% c("0", 0) ~ "HC",
      group %in% c("1", 1) ~ "FND",
      group %in% c("HC", "FND") ~ as.character(group),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("HC", "FND")),
    group_bin = ifelse(group == "FND", 1, 0),
    
    rs53576 = toupper(as.character(rs53576)),
    rs53576 = gsub("/", "", rs53576),
    rs53576 = gsub("\\|", "", rs53576),
    rs53576 = gsub(" ", "", rs53576),
    
    rs53576_add = case_when(
      rs53576 == "AA" ~ 0,
      rs53576 %in% c("AG", "GA") ~ 1,
      rs53576 == "GG" ~ 2,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(group_bin),
    !is.na(rs53576_add)
  )

# ℹ 2 more variables: OR_95CI_high <dbl>, p_observed <dbl>
#  simulation-based power for observed genetic association
simulate_genetic_case_control_power <- function(N, beta, geno_probs,
                                                case_fraction,
                                                nsim = 2000,
                                                alpha = 0.05) {
  
  
  # Find intercept so simulated FND proportion matches observed sample
  f_intercept <- function(intercept) {
    sum(plogis(intercept + beta * c(0, 1, 2)) * geno_probs) - case_fraction
  }
  
  intercept <- uniroot(f_intercept, interval = c(-20, 20))$root
  
  pvals <- replicate(nsim, {
    
    # simulate additive genotype according to observed genotype distribution
    genotype <- sample(
      x = c(0, 1, 2),
      size = N,
      replace = TRUE,
      prob = geno_probs
    )
    
    # simulate disease/group status from observed genetic effect
    prob_FND <- plogis(intercept + beta * genotype)
    group_bin <- rbinom(N, size = 1, prob = prob_FND)
    
    sim_dat <- data.frame(group_bin = group_bin,rs53576_add = genotype)
    
    fit <- try(
      glm(group_bin ~ rs53576_add, data = sim_dat, family = binomial),
      silent = TRUE
    )
    
    if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    
    coefs <- summary(fit)$coefficients
    
    if (!"rs53576_add" %in% rownames(coefs)) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    
    coefs["rs53576_add", "Pr(>|z|)"]
  })
  
  mean(pvals < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Observed genotype distribution
geno_probs_obs <- prop.table(table(df_genetic_power$rs53576_add))
geno_probs_obs <- as.numeric(geno_probs_obs[as.character(c(0, 1, 2))])
geno_probs_obs[is.na(geno_probs_obs)] <- 0

case_fraction_obs <- mean(df_genetic_power$group_bin == 1)

# Power across candidate sample sizes
N_grid <- seq(50, 2000, by = 25)

genetic_power_curve <- tibble(
  N_total = N_grid,
  power = sapply(
    N_grid,
    simulate_genetic_case_control_power,
    beta = beta_obs,
    geno_probs = geno_probs_obs,
    case_fraction = case_fraction_obs,
    nsim = 2000,
    alpha = 0.05
  )
)
